questions.question: If your motorcycle chain or belt breaks, what happens?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: When your chain or belt breaks, the rear wheel stops getting power right away.

questions.question: What should riders do when changing lanes?

options.text: Use only mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
Do not worry about other traffic.
Hit the brakes hard to let vehicles in your blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before you change lanes.

questions.question: What should a good face shield do?

options.text: Give you a clear view on both sides.
Stop air from passing through it.
Be so tight that glasses cannot fit under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a clear view on both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, let you see clearly to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and have room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: What should a face shield NOT do to be effective?

options.text: Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.explanation: A face shield should allow air to pass through. If it is airtight, it will fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: Which option gives the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you reduce crash risk?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.explanation: Be as visible as possible by wearing bright colors when you ride, even during the day.

questions.question: How can you tell if your rear tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing sound from the back.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When a rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You rarely hear a tire fail.

questions.question: What should you do if someone follows you too closely?

options.text: Focus on the road ahead and ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up makes it more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers do not expect you there.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when riding at night compared to riding during the day?

options.text: Allow more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase the space between you and other vehicles. Use headlights to see farther ahead. Never follow other vehicles too closely.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to make sure a driver will yield. A driver can look directly at you and still not actually see you.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing the front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions often to stay alert.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around your bike.
Never ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around your bike.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. The safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less frequent checking than a car.
More frequent checking than a car.
Pre-ride checks only by a mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent checking than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally recommended, groups should switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest and is operated by your left foot.

questions.question: How can you increase your ability to be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: To be seen at an intersection, ride with your headlight on and position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see it best. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can move quickly if needed. Do not assume eye contact alone will make a driver see you.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially hazardous because:

options.text: The front tire powers the bike, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire shakes the bike, making it hard to use mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Good protection includes a DOT-approved helmet, a jacket and long pants made of sturdy material, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and gloves made of durable material. A baseball cap does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: What material should motorcycle pants be made of for protection?

options.text: Material that flaps loosely in the wind
Short pants that expose the legs

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Learn the location of all motorcycle controls before you ride. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. Height does not affect BAC.
